input.exact_statement: Let d>=1 be an integer and A,B,C,D>0. For p_F(y)=sum_{j=0}^d (-1)^j binom(d,j)(A)_j(C)_j D^j y^j/[A^j C^j(B)_j(D)_j], where (x)_j is the rising factorial, assume A>=8B, B,D>=144d, 4d<=C-D<=D/4 and B/D<=4. Then p_F has d distinct positive roots. Every root and every real critical point satisfies |y-B|<10sqrt(Bd) and 9B/16<=y<=25B/16. For d=1 the only root is B and there are no critical points. Without the B/D restriction the original coarse assumptions alone imply no absolute sqrt(Bd) localization bound.
hypotheses: d is a positive integer and A,B,C,D are positive real numbers.
B/D<=4 is required for this repaired uniform constant.
